activities.anchor: Two creation texts frame the debate
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a stewardship briefing
activities.name: relStewardSpot

config.prompt: One line of this briefing on Christian environmental theology is wrong — click it:
lines: Genesis 1:28 ('have dominion') was long read as licence.
The stewardship reading pairs it with Genesis 2:15 — 'to till and keep it' — as trusteeship, not ownership.
Laudato Si' (2015) argued creation care, poverty and technology critique are one subject — 'the cry of the earth and the cry of the poor'.
Stewardship treats the earth as ownership, with no accountability attached.
config.correction: Stewardship is trusteeship, not ownership — humanity placed in the garden to till and keep it; a body of 2.4 billion adherents, landholdings, schools and pulpits is infrastructure the doctrine deploys.
config.why: The Church of England set a net-zero target for 2030; Eco Church schemes and divestment campaigns institutionalised the reading.

activities.caption: true or false — what shari'ah covers
activities.name: relShariaJudge

statements.s: Shari'ah's scope is mostly personal and devotional — worship, contracts, family and charity form the everyday core.
statements.why: Acts are classified from obligatory (the five pillars) through recommended, permitted, discouraged and forbidden.

statements.s: As economics, shari'ah prohibits riba (interest), producing a distinct Islamic-finance industry.
statements.why: Cost-plus murabaha contracts and profit-sharing; the maqasid al-sharia protect life, faith, intellect, lineage and property.

statements.s: Shari'ah is a single, uniform legal code applied identically everywhere.
statements.why: It is a civilisation-scale tradition of law and ethics: state criminal law in some countries, family-law codes in most Muslim-majority states, advisory councils in diasporas.

statements.s: Hudud penalties are a small, contested corner of the tradition.
statements.why: Applied in only some states and disputed by the majority of Muslim jurists historically — the headlines show the corner, not the whole.

activities.caption: drag the divider — two routes to trusteeship
activities.name: relKhalifaCompare

config.prompt: Two environmental theologies converge — drag the divider.

before.label: Christian stewardship
before.text: Genesis 1:28 paired with 2:15 — 'till and keep': trusteeship, not ownership. Laudato Si' folds creation care and poverty into one subject; institutional form followed in targets, schemes and divestment campaigns.

after.label: Khalifah
after.text: Humanity as God's vicegerent — trustees with accountability (Quran 2:30, 6:165). Mizan, the balance built into creation, which israf (waste) violates; the 2015 Istanbul declaration called for phasing out fossil emissions.

config.why: Khalifah re-reads 'dominion' exactly as Christian stewardship re-reads Genesis 1:28 — two traditions converging on trusteeship, with the environmental virtues already canonical, awaiting application.
